stories.title: 📜 Infancy Gospel of James
summaryBullets: Joachim, righteous yet childless, humbles himself through prayer and fasting, and Anna laments her barrenness (chapter 1).
An angel appears to Anna, announcing that she will conceive; Anna vows the child to the Lord’s service (chapter 2).
Joachim hears the promise as well, returns with abundant offerings, and Anna gives birth to a daughter named Mary (chapter 2).
As a child she grows strong; at age three, Joachim brings Mary to the Temple to fulfill her vow (chapter 7).
Mary is received by the high priest, placed on the temple steps, and anointed with divine favor (chapter 7).
She remains in the temple, receiving angelic food, and is cared for among the undefiled daughters of Israel (chapter 8).
When Mary reaches twelve, the priests seek a guardian for her (chapter 8).
All eligible widowers of Israel bring their rods to the altar for a sign from God (chapter 9).
Joseph’s rod miraculously blossoms, and a dove emerges, marking him as chosen (chapter 9).
Joseph, an older man, protests his unworthiness, but accepts guardianship of Mary (chapter 9).
The angel Gabriel appears to Mary, announcing she will conceive by the Holy Spirit (chapter 11).
Mary marvels at the message, asking how this can be, but submits to God’s will (chapter 11).
Joseph discovers her pregnancy and is troubled, fearing accusation (chapter 13).
An angel appears to Joseph in a dream, reassuring him that the child is of the Holy Spirit (chapter 14).
Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem for the census (chapter 17).
Mary is overtaken by labor, and they find a cave for shelter (chapter 18).
As Mary prepares to give birth, Joseph sees time miraculously stand still (chapter 18).
Mary gives birth in the cave, attended by a midwife (chapter 19).
A midwife named Salome doubts Mary’s virginity after childbirth (chapter 20).
When she tests Mary, her hand withers as punishment (chapter 20).
Salome cries out in pain, but is healed when she touches the infant Jesus (chapter 20).
The narrative closes with Mary’s purity confirmed and the child praised as the Savior.
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 1:10–11: Hannah prays for a child.
Luke 1:13–14: Angel announces birth of John the Baptist.
Luke 1:34–35: Mary’s virgin conception by Spirit.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֲקָרוֹת (ʿăqārôt), Greek: ἄτεκνος (áteknos), Aramaic: בלא זרעא (bela zērāʿā)
translationNotes.note: Describes the condition of being without children, seen in biblical narratives as a stigma reversed by divine blessing.

stories.keyTakeaway: Joachim and Anna’s faith and divine promise lead to the birth of Mary, dedicated to God from birth.
